thread.title: Apple: Just A Speed Bump? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Bill Maurer
title: Apple: Just A Speed Bump? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
The last couple of weeks have not been very good for shares of Apple ( AAPL ), which closed Monday down 6.2% from their all-time high. While markets have struggled a little recently, the Nasdaq has only declined by 3.5% from its high, so Apple has definitely underperformed. That gets us to today's question - is this just a speed bump or the start of something more?
Right now, the main concern seems to be over the Trump administration's stance regarding trade. The impact of tariffs, especially those regarding China, have been widely discussed. Last week there was some confusion over whether or not there would be an exemption for the iPhone. Greater China accounted for more than $13 billion in revenues for Apple during the March ending fiscal Q2 quarter, almost as much as all of Europe.
With iPhones being expensive enough in the overall smartphone space, any tariffs thrown on would obviously hurt demand. The other problem is if China were to make a larger push against American technology companies like Apple, perhaps encouraging consumers to only go with products from Chinese companies. I don't want to imagine a scenario where China starts subsidizing products from its own companies to hurt American firms.
The second item that could be an issue moving forward is the rebound in the US dollar. As seen by the euro-heavy Dollar Currency Index chart below, the greenback has done quite well in calendar Q2 after a couple weak quarters. While Apple does have a hedging program, it still can lose out a little in foreign markets thanks to dollar strength. Even a few hundred million in lost revenue could be the difference between a revenue beat or miss, as well as management perhaps lowering forward guidance a little from where it might have been when the DCI was at or below 90.
( Source: cnbc.com)
As we come to the end of the quarter, we're also seeing some index rebalancing that might play into things. Last week Apple lost some weight in the Russell rebalance, which may have resulted in some extra selling, and this week Apple will lose a little bit of weight in the Dow Jones Industrial Average as General Electric ( GE ) gets booted from the 30 member index .
The decline in Monday's trading may have led to a snowball effect for the recent pullback. As you can see in the chart below, shares fell below their 50-day moving average, a key level that may have caused some technical selling. Unfortunately, as the chart shows over the past few months, breaking below this key trend level has usually sent the stock down toward the 200-day moving average, which at this point would approach correction territory.
( Source: Yahoo Finance)
While investors never like to see a lot of red, those who were afraid to buy the rally above $190 may now have an opportunity in front of them. Shares are going for less than 14 times next fiscal year's projected earnings, a reasonable valuation, and you still are getting a 1.6% annual dividend plus the massive buyback. Should we get some of the usual pre-earnings analyst panic, a further decline to the 200-day moving average would make shares even more reasonable for investors.
With Apple shares pulling back a bit from their all-time highs, is this just a speed bump or the start of something more? It certainly seems like investors are worried about trade wars, which definitely could hurt Apple given its reliance on China. However, don't ignore the rising dollar, index rebalancing, and the breach of the 50-day. I think Apple remains in solid shape for the long term, so if we do get down to the longer term trend line, investors should consider the opportunity.
